_comment: Basic 2:1 serializer from J. Kim et al., JSSC 54(1), Jan. 2019, Fig. 4(b), DOI:10.1109/JSSC.2018.2874040.

Time axis is in units of Tck. One wave character is Tck/8; period=0.5 makes its horizontal width 20px. Divider starts low and first rises after the CK edge at t=0. Initial divider phase is a chosen example, not a specified reset state.
d0=a,c,e and d1=b,d,f are paired parallel inputs, stable before their common CKdiv rising-edge capture. Q0 is the upper d0 FF; Q1a is the first lower d1 FF; Q1b is the second lower d1 FF.

Q0 and Q1a capture on rising CKdiv. Q1b captures Q1a on falling CKdiv. Output captures the pre-edge mux value on rising CK. Top-facing clock triangles are still positive-edge; the bubble on Q1b makes it negative-edge.
The upper TG has an active-low control: CKdiv=0 selects Q0; CKdiv=1 selects Q1b. Each selected register was loaded on the opposite CKdiv edge.

Illustrative delays only: tdiv=Tck/8, tmux=Tck/4, FF clock-to-Q=Tck/8, assumed tsu=Tck/8. These are not paper measurements. CKdiv edges follow CK rising edges by tdiv. Input data FF clock-to-Q is shown as well.
The output therefore becomes a,b,c,d at 2Tck+tcq,3Tck+tcq,4Tck+tcq,5Tck+tcq. Mux a is ready at Tck+tdiv+tmux and sampled at 2Tck.
The critical clock-to-select-to-data path has tdiv+tmux+tsu<Tck; at the 8:4 stage Tck=4UI. Hatched regions omit earlier data; they are not a reset prescription.
Waveforms were generated by an event-driven model of the displayed FFs, divide-by-two select, and mux, with pre-edge output sampling. Local WaveDrom Editor 3.7.0 renderer.
The setup-window arrow runs from mux=c settling at 3Tck+tdiv+tmux to its capture edge at 4Tck. Output Q becomes c only after the output FF clock-to-Q delay.
Time-axis labels use explicit strings; zero-width spaces leave the quarter-period minor ticks unlabeled.

foot.text: Time / Tck. Delays illustrative.  t_div + t_mux + t_su < Tck
